L9: # Register your interest in our dog cancer trial
L10: 
L11: We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.
L12: 
L13: 【5†Register your interest  →】 【8†See how it works  →】
L14: 
L15: Why we are running this trial
L16: ## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.
L17: 
L18: 【9†Image: Rosie】
L19: 
L20: Rosie
L21: 
L22: The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.
L23: 
L24: It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.
L25: Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.
L26: 
L27: 【2†Read Rosie’s personalised mRNA cancer-vaccine story  →】
L28: 
L29: Who can register
L30: ## If your dog has cancer and is currently in Australia, you’re welcome to register your interest. Our team will check whether your dog may be eligible for this trial.
L31: 
L32: 【5†Register your interest  →】
L33: 
L34: About the trial
L35: 
L36: ## What this trial is looking at
L37: 
L38: The trial will investigate a personalised mRNA vaccine approach for dogs with mast cell cancer. Tell us about your dog and our team will help determine whether they may be eligible for screening.
L39: 
L40: 【10†Image】
L41: ### Who can register
L42: 
L43: Dogs diagnosed with mast cell cancer who are based in, or able to travel within, Australia.
L44: 
L45: Every case is reviewed individually
L46: 
L47: 【11†Image】
L48: 
L49: ### The trial approach
L50: 
L51: A therapeutic mRNA vaccine designed from each dog’s own tumour and blood samples, intended to work alongside—not replace—existing care.
L52: 
L53: Personalised to each dog
L54: 
L55: 【12†Image】
L56: ### What screening involves
L57: 
L58: We help coordinate records, screening, sample logistics and updates, working with the trial team and your treating veterinarian.
L59: 
L60: A named team stays in touch
L61: 
L62: Trial registration and screening
L63: 
L64: ## How to register your interest.
L65: 
L66: You don’t need to have every record ready before registering your interest. Start with what you know and we’ll help with the rest.
L67: 
L68: 01
L69: ### Register your interest
L70: 
L71: Complete a short form with basic details about your dog, their mast cell cancer diagnosis and where you live.
L72: 
L73: 02
L74: 
L75: ### We get in touch
L76: 
L77: A Gamgee coordinator will contact you, answer practical questions and—with your permission—help gather relevant records from your vet.
L78: 
L79: 03
L80: ### The trial team confirms eligibility
L81: 
L82: The authorised study team and treating veterinarian assess potential eligibility. If your dog may proceed, you’ll receive the approved trial information and consent discussion before deciding.
L83: 
L84: These are indicative timings from a single case. Sequencing turnaround and manufacturing schedules may vary. We will give you a case-specific estimate before proceeding.
L85: 
L86: 【13†Image: A dog looking up at the camera】
L87: ## Ready to tell us about your dog?
L88: 
L89: Registering your interest does not guarantee eligibility or enrolment. Please continue your dog's existing veterinary care while your information is reviewed.
L90: 
L91: 【5†Register your interest  →】

L160: ## Clinical Research
L161: 
L162: ## Clinical Research at MediPaws
L163: ##### Our commitment to advancing the field of veterinary medicine
L164: 
L165: Advancing veterinary care is about delivering the best care today while learning how to improve care for future patients. Much like in human medicine, clinical research plays an important role in helping veterinarians refine treatments, reduce risk, and achieve better patient outcomes.
L166: Many of the treatments and approaches used at MediPaws and other veterinary hospitals have been shaped by ongoing research. Through these evidence-based findings, we are able to continually improve the safety and effectiveness of care for our beloved pets.
L167: ##### Why participate in clinical research
L168: 
L169: Many pet owners participate in clinical research knowing that their pet’s involvement may help improve care for other pets in the future. By participating in our no-harm studies, your pet can contribute to better treatments, reduced procedure risk, and improved quality of life for pets in the future around the world.
L170: Each study will provide specific information about any potential benefits for your pet. Depending on the research, this may include additional insight into recovery, monitoring, or complementary diagnostic testing.
L171: 
L172: Why we're involved in clinical research​
L173: At MediPaws, clinical research is a natural extension of our commitment to provide the highest standard of care possible. Every day, our teams manage complex emergency and referral cases across multiple specialties, giving us valuable insight into how treatments perform in real-world settings and what works best.
L174: 
L175: Clinical research allows our specialists to keep asking important questions, including:
L176:   * How can we improve tests and treatments already in use?
L177:   * Can we reduce risks around anaesthesia, hospitalisation and recovery?
L178:   * What can we do to improve long-term outcomes and quality of life for patients?
L179: 
L180: What “no-harm” clinical research means at MediPaws
L181: Our specialists take a no-harm approach to all clinical research, meaning every study is designed with patient welfare as the top priority. Research is carefully structured so it never compromises care, and often involves non-invasive data collection alongside routine treatment or comparing standard approaches already in use.
L182: 
L183: Participation in any research at MediPaws is always:
L184:   * Voluntary – clear explanations are provided, and informed consent is required
L185:   * Ethics-approved – studies follow appropriate governance and ethics processes
L186:   * Patient-first – your pet’s clinical care always takes precedence over research
L187: 
L188: What does taking part in a study mean for your pet?
L189: 
L190: If your pet is eligible for a clinical study, express your interest on our study page and a member of the MediPaws team will discuss it with you in detail. As a part of this, we’ll explain:
L191:   * What the study is aiming to achieve
L192:   * What (if anything) will be different from standard care
L193:   * Answers to any questions you may have before you decide to take part
L194: 
L195: In most cases, participation does not change your pet’s treatment plan. Your pet will continue to receive the same high standard of veterinary care, monitoring, and support they would receive outside of a study. You are also free to withdraw from a study at any time, without affecting your pet’s care in any way.
L196: Your pet’s comfort, safety, and wellbeing will always be our first priority.
